new_statements.quote: While the normal vowels are used for soft sound, the accented vowels are used for stressed sound. [Rule 1:] Whenever hard vowels are required, Rohingyalish uses another set of vowels (á, é, í, ó, ú), which are normally known as accented (gutá) vowels. [...] Bak = tiger / Bák = share; Bet = cane stick / Bét = intention; Kil = punch / Kíl = wedge; Zor = fever / Zór = rain; Ful = hole/bridge / Fúl = flower. [Rule 2:] Rohingyalish has a total of (12) basic vowels where six are of the soft-sounds and the other six are of hard-sounds.

Every clause of the quotation is present at the stated locators: intro paragraph 'While the normal vowels are used for soft sound, the accented vowels are used for stressed sound.'; Rule 1 heading 'The original English vowels (a, e, i, o, u) are used as soft vowels.' and body 'Whenever hard vowels are required, Rohingyalish uses another set of vowels (á, é, í, ó, ú), which are normally known as accented (gutá) vowels.'; the Rule 1 example table Bak=tiger / Bák=share, Bet=cane stick / Bét=intention, Kil=punch / Kíl=wedge, Zor=fever / Zór=rain, Ful=hole/bridge / Fúl=f…
new_statements.relation_note: The catalog record for Rohingya has an empty rule and there are no existing statements, so nothing to agree or disagree with. This source adds that the Rohingyalish orthography marks a lexical 'stressed/hard' vs 'soft' vowel contrast with an acute accent, contrastive even in monosyllables; it does not supply a word-stress placement rule, so the catalog rule should stay empty (or be marked as an orthographic vowel-register contrast, not positional stress).
new_statements.rule_in_words: The work is an orthography guide, not a phonological description. It says the acute-accented vowels á é í ó ú write a 'stressed' or 'hard' sound and the plain vowels a e i o u a 'soft' (and short) sound, giving twelve fixed vowel sounds, and it shows the contrast with minimal pairs that are monosyllables (Bak 'tiger' vs Bák 'share', Zor 'fever' vs Zór 'rain'). So what it calls stress is a lexical vowel contrast marked on any vowel of any syllable (examples: Sultán, Fonná, Hañdá, Cúndor, Sáda, Kurá, Córom, Goró, Hóro, Thalasabí, and once two accented vowels in one word, Óroói 'grain for mustard oil'), not a statement about which syllable of a word is prominent. It gives no rule for word-stress placement, no claim that stress is absent, and no mention of tone.
new_statements.exceptions: none stated about accent; the only dialect remark is that h-initial vs vowel-initial doublets (áñti / háñti 'elephant', áñc / háñc 'duck') differ between north and south Arakan (Rule 7)
new_statements.identity_note: The work describes 'Rohingyalish', the Rohingya Language Foundation's Latin orthography for Rohingya of Arakan State (Rakhine), Myanmar; no dialect is specified for the vowel system, and the only dialect remark concerns north vs south Arakan h-initial doublets (Rule 7).

tone_statements.citation: The Unicode Consortium. 2024. The Unicode Standard, Version 16.0 -- Core Specification. Chapter 16 'Southeast Asia-I', section 'Hanifi Rohingya: U+10D00-U+10D3F' (and Chapter 9, 'Arabic Extended-A' block note on Rohingya Fonna tone marks). South San Francisco, CA: Unicode Consortium. HTML edition.
tone_statements.quote: Vowels are expressed using five letter-like vowel signs (U+10D1D..U+10D21) placed after a consonant. These vowel signs represent short vowels. Vowel length and stress are indicated by three tone signs placed above vowel signs: U+10D24 HANIFI ROHINGYA SIGN HARBAHAY U+10D25 HANIFI ROHINGYA SIGN TAHALA U+10D26 HANIFI ROHINGYA SIGN TANA ... The consonant gemination sign U+10D27 HANIFI ROHINGYA SIGN TASSI indicates doubled consonants. When both the tassi and a tonal sign are present, the tassi is placed first and the tonal sign is displayed visually to its left.

sources.citation: Priest, Lorna A. & Martin Hosken (SIL International). 2010. Proposal to add Arabic script characters for African and Asian languages (revised). Unicode Technical Committee document L2/10-288R, 2010-08-12. Unicode Consortium. PDF, 4.7 MB.
sources.note: The Arabic-script Rohingya Fonna orthography writes three tone marks (tone 1 single dot, tone 2 double dot, tone 3 loop) above or below the vowel sign; the pitch values of the tones are not described.

tone.quote: Tone marks in the Rohingya language form the ‘outer layer’ of the script (i.e. above Fatha, Damma, etc, and below Kasra2, etc.). … The rule is: if a letter has a vowel symbol that is positioned above the consonant, then the tone mark goes above the vowel symbol. If the vowel symbol is below the consonant, then the tone mark goes below the vowel symbol (tone marks will never appear if there is no vowel symbol). … For the tone marks, sorting should have a secondary weight and sort as follows: (1) unmarked vowel, (2) single dot tone mark, (3) double dot tone mark, (4) looped tone mark.
